relationships.subject: gabapentinoids
relationships.evidence_quote: These agents act by targeting the α2δ subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels, leading to decreased neuronal excitability [8].

relationships.subject: capsaicin
relationships.evidence_quote: The 5% lidocaine patches act by blocking sodium channels, and high-dose capsaicin works through TRPV1 receptor desensitization [8].

relationships.subject: ketamine
relationships.evidence_quote: Ketamine, a noncompetitive NMDA receptor antagonist, disrupts this pathway by blocking calcium entry, thereby dampening nociceptive transmission.

relationships.subject: TLR4/NF-κB pathway
relationships.evidence_quote: Xue et al. identified that the TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway is a downstream regulator of S100A4 activation, and that specific depletion of this pathway suppresses deleterious A1 astrocyte activation and further attenuates the development and maintenance of neuropathic pain [22].

key_findings: Tiered neuropathic pain treatment: gabapentinoids/TCAs/SNRIs first-line, topical agents and tramadol second-line, NMDA antagonists, cannabinoids, botulinum toxin third-line.
S100A4/TLR4/NF-κB signaling in astrocytes is an emerging analgesic target.
